trial_name.text: KL4-IRDS-06 (Study 1), the single pivotal efficacy study

citations.quote: The original application included the results of a single pivotal study (study KL4-IRDS-06) which established the efficacy and safety of lucinactant for the proposed indication, “the prevention of RDS in premature infants”. Th
KL4-IRDS-06 was the single pivotal study upon which clinical support for the indication rested.

phase.text: Pivotal prophylaxis superiority trial (major efficacy study)

citations.quote: KL4-IRDS-06 was a multinational (Europe and Latin America), multicenter (50 active centers), randomized, masked, active-controlled (Survanta®), prophylaxis superiority trial of the safety and effectiveness of Surfaxin® compared to Exosurf® in the prevention of RDS in premature neonates.

design.text: Multicenter, multinational, randomized, double-blind, multi-dose, active-controlled superiority study comparing SURFAXIN to colfosceril palmitate (Exosurf), with beractant (Survanta) as an additional active comparator

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of SURFAXIN for the prevention of RDS in premature infants was demonstrated in a single randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled, multi-dose study involving 1294 premature infants (Study 1).

The demonstration of efficacy was provided by study KL4-IRDS-06, a multicenter, multinational, randomized study conducted outside the United States that compared Surfaxin® to Exosurf in a superiority design. A second active comparator, Survanta, was included for reference.

population.text: Premature infants weighing 600 g to 1250 g at birth and 32 weeks or less gestational age, at high risk for RDS; participants from Europe and Latin America

citations.quote: This study included 646 males and 648 females who weighed between 600 g and 1250 g at birth and were 32 weeks or less in gestational age. Seventy-eight percent of the infants were white, 1% black, and 21% classified as other. Study participants were from Europe and Latin America.

endpoint.text: Co-primary endpoints: incidence of RDS at 24 hours and RDS-related mortality through Day 14, with SURFAXIN vs. colfosceril palmitate (Exosurf) as the primary comparison for superiority

citations.quote: Co-primary endpoints were the incidence of RDS (defined as having a chest x-ray consistent with RDS and an \text{FiO}_2 \geq 0.30) at 24 hours and RDS-related mortality at 14 days. The primary comparison of interest was between SURFAXIN and colfosceril palmitate with the intent of demonstrating superiority.

n.text: 1294 premature infants (SURFAXIN N=527, colfosceril palmitate N=509, beractant N=258)

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of SURFAXIN for the prevention of RDS in premature infants was demonstrated in a single randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled, multi-dose study involving 1294 premature infants (Study 1).
infants were randomized to receive 1 of 3 surfactants, SURFAXIN (N = 527), colfosceril palmitate (N = 509), or beractant (N = 258).

result.text: SURFAXIN was superior to colfosceril palmitate on both co-primary endpoints: RDS at 24 hours 206 (39%) vs 240 (47%), P<0.01; RDS-related mortality through Day 14 25 (5%) vs 48 (9%), P<0.01. Reviewer analysis: 17% risk reduction in RDS at 24h (95% CI 5%, 28%; p=0.007) and 52% reduction in RDS-related mortality by 14 days (95% CI 24%, 69%; p=0.001).

citations.quote: RDS-related mortality through Day 1425 (5)48 (9)<0.01

Surfaxin yielded a statistically significant reduction (17%, 95% Confidence limit: 5%, 28%, p=0.007 reviewer's analysis based on the Agency's agreed and protocol specified stratified CMH test, p=0.005 sponsor's logistic regression stratifying on center and birthweight) in RDS incidence at 24 hours of age, a statistically significant reduction (52%, 95%CI: 24%, 69%, p=0.001 CMH test or logistic method) in RDS related mortality by 14 days.

indication.text: Prevention of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants at high risk for RDS; reduces the incidence of RDS at 24 hours and mortality due to RDS

citations.quote: SURFAXIN® (lucinactant) Intratracheal Suspension is indicated for the prevention of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants at high risk for RDS. SURFAXIN reduces the incidence of RDS at 24 hours and mortality due to RDS.

target_moa.text: A synthetic lung surfactant that compensates for the deficiency of endogenous pulmonary surfactant in premature infants, lowering surface tension at the alveolar air-liquid interface and stabilizing alveoli against collapse; contains sinapultide (KL4 peptide) which mimics surfactant protein B (SP-B)

citations.quote: Endogenous pulmonary surfactant lowers surface tension at the air-liquid interface of the alveolar surfaces during respiration and stabilizes the alveoli against collapse at resting transpulmonary pressures. A deficiency of pulmonary surfactant in premature infants results in RDS. SURFAXIN compensates for the deficiency of surfactant and restores surface activity to the lungs of these infants.
Surfaxin (lucinactant) is a novel peptide-containing synthetic surfactant that mimics the essential characteristics of human surfactant protein B (SP-B).

modality.text: Peptide-containing synthetic pulmonary surfactant (contains sinapultide, a 21-amino acid synthetic KL4 peptide)

citations.quote: It is a synthetic formulation consisting of phospholipids, a fatty acid, and sinapultide (KL4 peptide), a 21-amino acid hydrophobic synthetic peptide.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions are administration-related: endotracheal tube reflux, pallor, endotracheal tube obstruction, and need for dose interruption, which occurred at higher incidence with SURFAXIN than comparator surfactants (e.g., Study 1 ETT reflux 18% vs 16%; pallor 9% vs 4%; dose interruption 9% vs 4%; ETT obstruction 6% vs 2%). Frequently occurring administration-related reactions include bradycardia, oxygen desaturation, reflux into the ETT, and airway/ETT obstruction.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions associated with the use of SURFAXIN are endotracheal tube reflux, pallor, endotracheal tube obstruction, and need for dose interruption. (6.1)
Frequently occurring adverse reactions related to the administration of SURFAXIN include bradycardia, oxygen desaturation, reflux of drug into the endotracheal tube (ETT), and airway/ETT obstruction.

detail.text: No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies (REMS) are recommended

citations.quote: No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended.

vote.text: No advisory committee was convened; the Agency determined outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

citations.quote: Your application for lucinactant was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

detail.text: Not a first-cycle approval; this was a later review cycle. The original NDA was submitted April 13, 2004; FDA issued an Approvable letter February 11, 2005 and an action (Complete Response) letter April 17, 2009, before approval (the September 2, 2011 submission constituted a complete response to the April 17, 2009 action letter; the approval letter was signed March 6, 2012).

citations.quote: This is the fourth review cycle for Surfaxin (lucinactant) Intratracheal Suspension (NDA 21-746), which was originally submitted by Discovery Laboratories on April 13, 2004.

On February 11, 2005, the Division took an Approvable action on the application. The clinical recommendation was Approval, but there were substantial CMC deficiencies that resulted in the Approvable action.
The September 2, 2011, submission constituted a complete response to our April 17, 2009, action letter.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received April 13, 2004, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Surfaxin (lucinactant) Intratracheal Suspension.

basis.text: Chemistry/manufacturing: the submission had not adequately addressed the deficiency of validating an in vivo rabbit fetal model, as the rabbit bioassay was not sensitive enough to discriminate between active and inactive (degraded) drug product

citations.quote: This submission has not adequately addressed the deficiency of validating an in vivo rabbit fetal model
the Division stated that we continued to have concerns over the ability of the rabbit bioassay to discriminate between active and inactive drug product as described earlier in this review.

orphan_indication.text: SURFAXIN has an orphan drug designation for this indication (prevention of RDS in premature infants), an orphan disease

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
Surfaxin, like other surfactants for the prevention or treatment of RDS in premature infants has an orphan designation.

summary.text: SURFAXIN (lucinactant) was a 505(b)(2) NDA with orphan drug designation for prevention of RDS in premature infants. It was approved after multiple review cycles (originally submitted April 13, 2004; Approvable letter February 11, 2005; Complete Response action letter April 17, 2009; approval letter signed March 6, 2012), based on a single pivotal superiority study (KL4-IRDS-06) versus colfosceril palmitate. No advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received April 13, 2004, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Surfaxin (lucinactant) Intratracheal Suspension.

On February 11, 2005, the Division took an Approvable action on the application. The clinical recommendation was Approval, but there were substantial CMC deficiencies that resulted in the Approvable action.
The September 2, 2011, submission constituted a complete response to our April 17, 2009, action letter.

The demonstration of efficacy was provided by study KL4-IRDS-06, a multicenter, multinational, randomized study conducted outside the United States that compared Surfaxin® to Exosurf in a superiority design. A second active comparator, Survanta, was included for reference.
